field_lens: Research and engineering ethics, applied through a language-science society's peer-review system.
ai_connection: Every NLP and LLM paper submitted through ACL Rolling Review must discuss malicious or unintended harmful effects, dual use, risks to fairness, privacy and security, and any use of AI assistants. It is a field-wide norm-setting tool aimed at language-model research. Caveat: computational linguistics overlaps heavily with mainstream ML.

name: International Federation of Translators (FIT): Working Group on AI Ethics and AI position papers
one_line: The global federation of translator, interpreter and terminologist associations. Since 2024 it has published position papers on AI in interpreting and on machine translation in the age of AI, and in August 2026 a report on AI ethics in translation and interpreting.
field_lens: Professional translation and interpreting practice and its ethics codes. MISFIT: no linguistics or translation tradition exists in the taxonomy, so it is placed under arts (communications).
ai_connection: The AI Ethics Working Group sets out six principles for using AI in translation and interpreting. It insists on human oversight in high-stakes settings (courts, healthcare, diplomacy), and calls for transparency and labelling. It also warns governments against unsupervised AI translation and interpreting. These are oversight norms drawn from a profession that has long managed meaning-critical risk.

name: Chartered Institute of Linguists (CIOL): CIOL & AI
one_line: The UK chartered professional body for linguists. It runs a standing AI resource hub (AI Voices 2025, AI Updates) and commissioned research on AI translation in UK public services, presented to the APPG on Modern Languages in June 2025.
field_lens: Applied linguistics and the professional practice of translators and interpreters. MISFIT: no linguistics tradition, so it is placed under arts (communications).
ai_connection: A Bristol study it commissioned surveyed 2,500 frontline workers and found that a third use AI translation, including for medical consent forms and child-protection work. It documents high-risk, unsupervised AI use in public services and pushes for safeguards. It also shares corpus research on how LLM text differs from human writing.

name: Institute of Translation and Interpreting (ITI): AI policy
one_line: UK professional association for translators and interpreters. It keeps a policy line and resource hub on generative AI, and endorses the FIT and European Language Council AI papers.
field_lens: Translation and interpreting profession. MISFIT: placed under arts (communications).
ai_connection: Light engagement: a board-level AI policy holding that humans remain essential for accurate and ethical outcomes, plus a curated hub of AI ethics papers. Transferable method: professional quality and ethics standards for meaning-critical language work, usable as human-oversight norms for AI translation.

name: European Language Council (CEL/ELC)
location: Secretariat at Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore, Milan, Italy
one_line: European association for language policy in higher education. In November 2025 it published 'AI for Translation and Interpreting: A Roadmap for Users and Policy Makers', and in April 2026 it held a seminar titled '(De)Generative AI and Multilingual (Mis)Communication'.
field_lens: Language policy, multilingualism and translation-studies education. MISFIT: placed under arts.
ai_connection: The roadmap explains to lay users and policymakers how LLMs 'communicate' differently from humans, and what side effects to weigh. Engagement is light. Transferable method: a language-policy framework for multilingual communication risk and for training professionals around AI.

name: Interpreting SAFE AI Task Force (Stakeholders Advocating for Fair and Ethical AI in Interpreting)
one_line: Independent multi-stakeholder task force of interpreters, the American Translators Association, CoSET, vendors and end users. It publishes guidance and an AI Interpreting Solutions Evaluation Toolkit (2025) for safe, fair and ethical machine interpreting.
field_lens: Professional interpreting practice, spoken and signed, treated as a sociotechnical communication system. MISFIT: placed under arts (communications).
ai_connection: Writes evaluation and risk-governance standards for AI interpreting. Its toolkit rejects judging only the language model's performance; it also covers human participants, legal and medical context, and accountability and liability. It is an assurance framework for a high-stakes deployment, written by language professionals. Still active in May 2026.

name: CoSET (Coalition for Sign Language Equity in Technology)
one_line: Sign-language community coalition (#DeafSafeAI), pending incorporation as a 501(c)(3). It co-developed the SAFE AI interpreting toolkit and runs workshops on assessing AI sign-language interpreting.
field_lens: Deaf community and sign-language linguistics, through a language-rights and disability-rights lens.
ai_connection: Advocates standardised safety checklists for buyers of AI interpreting, and asks developers to co-design with signers and interpreters to anticipate failure modes. In March 2026 it promoted the toolkit with SAFE AI. It protects a linguistic minority from unsafe automated interpreting.

name: Association des traducteurs littéraires de France (ATLF): generative-AI clauses
one_line: French literary translators' association. In December 2024 it added three generative-AI clauses to its model publishing contract: no AI for the translation, no AI in exploiting the rights, and an opt-out from training. It campaigns on publishers' moves to AI (Harlequin, December 2025).
field_lens: Literary translation as a profession, defending its working conditions and moral rights.
ai_connection: Uses contract standards to refuse AI translation and to block use of translators' work as training data. It is a bottom-up governance instrument over training data and AI substitution in publishing.

name: Collectif En chair et en os
one_line: French grassroots collective of translators ('Oui à l'humain, non à l'IA'). It organised an anti-AI summit in Lille (June 2026) and an international translators' strike day on 30 September 2026, held in Aubervilliers and Lyon and joined by groups in Spain.
field_lens: Organised translators and literary workers, refusing AI substitution of human language work.
ai_connection: Organises collective action against AI replacing translation and against how AI is rolled out in culture. It is a labour and refusal stance on the pace of automation, with 2026 actions and a counter-summit to a regional AI summit.

name: Rising Voices (Global Voices): Indigenous languages, AI accountability and self-determination
location: Distributed (Global Voices); programmes in Mexico and Latin America
one_line: Global Voices initiative supporting digital activism in marginalised and Indigenous languages. In 2025-26 it ran AI accountability work with Mayan-language activists in Chiapas and reported on AI's language gaps.
field_lens: Indigenous-language digital activism and self-determination: a community language-rights tradition.
ai_connection: A hybrid peer programme (2026, supported by the Kellogg Foundation and the Pulitzer Center) on AI literacy and AI accountability from Indigenous perspectives. It addresses extraction of Indigenous language data without consent and communities' right to decide whether AI enters their languages. Also: reporting that AI content moderation covers fewer than 20 of Africa's 2,000 languages.

name: Welsh Language Commissioner: AI and the Welsh Language regulatory policy statement
one_line: Statutory language regulator for Wales. It has issued a regulatory policy statement on AI: organisations using AI for public services must still meet their Welsh-language duties.
field_lens: Minority-language rights law and language regulation.
ai_connection: Applies the precautionary principle to AI. Organisations must test AI systems specifically in Welsh, be transparent about how the systems work, and meet standards of linguistic fairness and accuracy. It is a working template for regulating AI's effects on a minority language.

name: Språkrådet (Language Council of Norway): Språkteknologi og KI
one_line: Norway's state language authority. It has a standing language technology and AI programme: language requirements for public-sector digital and AI products, sharing Bokmål and Nynorsk language data, and advice on AI writing tools.
field_lens: Language law and language planning for a small national language and its minority written standard.
ai_connection: Sets requirements for owners, buyers and developers of language-technology products in the public sector, and organises Norwegian data for AI. It is a state-level response to the risk that AI weakens smaller languages.

name: SIL Global: AI Ethics Statement
one_line: Faith-based field-linguistics and Bible-translation organisation working with minority-language communities. It has an AI and NLP ethics framework built on 'Just, Kind, Humble' and on informed consent for language data.
field_lens: Christian mission linguistics (the framing echoes Micah 6:8) combined with field documentation of minority languages.
ai_connection: A single statement that appears to date from about 2022-23, judging by the sources it cites. It commits to benefit local language communities, consent and data minimisation for language data, and avoiding personifying AI. Transferable method: consent and community-benefit protocols for low-resource-language data used in AI.

name: Foundation for Endangered Languages (FEL)
location: UK charity; 2026 conference at INALCO, Paris
one_line: UK charity supporting endangered-language documentation and revitalisation. Its 30th conference, with INALCO in Paris on 3-5 November 2026, is on 'Endangered Languages and Innovative Technologies'.
field_lens: Documentary linguistics and community-led language revitalisation.
ai_connection: Engagement is light, through one conference. Its theme statement criticises technologies built on dominant-language data and argues for community data sovereignty and treating endangered languages as places where technology's assumptions get challenged. Transferable method: community-centred, consent-based documentation ethics for minority-language data in AI.

name: Cambridge Language Sciences Interdisciplinary Research Centre: 'Improving Language Equity and Inclusion through AI'
one_line: University of Cambridge network spanning psycholinguistics, neuroscience, applied linguistics and computer science. It runs a two-year AI@Cam project (to September 2026) that funds AI-focused workshops on language equity, and held a symposium on hate-speech detection in the age of AI (January 2026).
field_lens: Language sciences: psycholinguistics, clinical aphasiology, language assessment and sociolinguistics.
ai_connection: A time-limited programme with workshops on AI in aphasia recovery, human-AI collaboration in language assessment, and critical limits of AI hate-speech detection. Transferable method: evaluating whose language and speech AI serves well or badly.

name: BAAL Humans, Machines, Language (HuMaLa) Special Interest Group
location: UK (BAAL); events in the UK and Spain
one_line: British Association for Applied Linguistics SIG founded in March 2024. It succeeds the 2020-24 COST network 'Language in the Human-Machine Era' (LITHME) and studies the opportunities and risks of language technologies that merge humans and machines. Free and open to all.
field_lens: Applied linguistics and sociolinguistics of human-machine communication. MISFIT: no linguistics tradition, so it is placed under law_sts.
ai_connection: Research network and conferences (an inaugural conference, then 2026 events in Granada and Surrey) offering critical analysis of AI assistants, translation, language policy and literacies. It is the main applied-linguistics venue on AI's effects on human language.

name: Royal Statistical Society (RSS): AI Task Force
one_line: The UK's learned society and professional body for statisticians. Its AI Task Force argues that evaluating and regulating AI is largely a statistical problem.
field_lens: Statistics: inference, experimental design and uncertainty quantification, applied to evaluating and regulating AI. MISFIT: the taxonomy has no statistics sub-tradition, so the nearest home is Formal.
ai_connection: The AI Task Force exists to 'communicate the importance of statistics to the effective, ethical and safe use of AI'; it put out a call for members on 15 Sept 2026. Its 2026 policy papers are 'AI is Statistics' and 'Regulating AI' (AI regulation needs statistical capability). A policy blog of 30 Sept 2026 argues that regulating AI is mostly a matter of evaluating models as they operate in deployment, and reports talks with sector regulators in health, education and finance. The RSS also publishes the journal RSS: Data Science and Artificial Intelligence. The ring is borderline between bridge and adjacent: the framing is safety and evaluation, but the focus is sector regulation rather than frontier risk.

name: American Statistical Association (ASA): ethical AI statement and AI-in-pharma risk symposium
one_line: The US professional society for statisticians. It issued an ethical-AI statement for statistical practitioners in 2024 and co-sponsors an annual symposium on the risks of AI in pharmaceutical medicine.
field_lens: Statistical practice and professional ethics: auditing, validation, model governance. MISFIT: nearest home is Formal.
ai_connection: The 'ASA Statement on Ethical AI Principles for Statistical Practitioners' (8 Oct 2024) treats trustworthiness as the overall goal, including safety, reliability, validity and human-in-the-loop oversight. Its accountability principle says statisticians must be able to audit, monitor and evaluate AI, and must ensure there is a system for assessing and reducing AI risks. The ASA co-sponsors the Annual Symposium on Risks and Opportunities of AI in Pharmaceutical Medicine (2026 edition at UC Berkeley, Oct 2026) and earlier published a statement on the role of statistics in data science and AI.

name: National Physical Laboratory (NPL): Centre for AI Measurement
one_line: A new national centre at the UK's metrology institute, building the measurement science for testing, evaluating and assuring AI systems.
field_lens: Metrology: traceability, uncertainty budgets and comparability of measurements, applied to AI testing and assurance.
ai_connection: The Centre for AI Measurement launches officially on 10 Nov 2026 at Teddington. It covers measurement foundations for AI testing and evaluation, uncertainty quantification, validation and verification, and real-world monitoring. Its call for evidence on AI testing, evaluation and assurance in the UK closes 9 Oct 2026, and the work follows DSIT's Trusted Third-Party AI Assurance Roadmap (Sept 2025). NPL also takes part in the UK AI Standards Hub. Ring is bridge: an old metrology institution with a standing AI-assurance programme.

name: PTB Competence Centre 'AI and Metrology' (AI-Met)
one_line: A competence centre at Germany's national metrology institute, set up in January 2025, that applies metrological rigour to AI test datasets, benchmarks and uncertainty quantification.
field_lens: Metrology and measurement uncertainty, applied to AI benchmarks, test datasets and conformity assessment.
ai_connection: Set up on 17 Jan 2025. With Fraunhofer IAIS it led DIN SPEC 92007 (June 2026), general requirements for AI test datasets, which responds to the AI Act's Article 15 call for benchmarks and measurement methods; it was also involved in DIN SPEC 92006 (Feb 2026). U-TraCE (Jan 2026) uses conformal prediction as an evaluation tool that gives a formal upper bound on a black-box model's error probability. It hosted the MAITRE 2025 workshop (Metrics for Measurement of AI for Trustworthy, Reliable and Explainable Applications) at PTB Berlin in July 2025, and an 'Operationalizing the AI Act' panel at the QI-Digital Forum in Oct 2025.

name: IEEE Reliability Society: TRUE AI Initiative
one_line: A cross-disciplinary initiative of the IEEE Reliability Society for Trustworthy, Robust, Understandable and Explainable AI in reliability-critical and safety-critical systems.
field_lens: Reliability engineering and statistics (failure analysis, prognostics, fault tolerance, verification and validation), applied to AI assurance.
ai_connection: Its focus areas include verification, validation and assurance of AI models; robust and fault-tolerant ML; standards and metrics for AI-system reliability; secure, self-recovering AI; and human-AI teaming. Planned outputs are workshops, a roadmap, position papers, standards work, a TRUE AI column in Reliability Magazine and special issues of IEEE Transactions on Reliability. The steering committee includes Jeff Voas, and the Society's homepage promotes the initiative in 2026. The page gives no launch date.

name: Harding Center for Risk Literacy
one_line: A Potsdam research centre in the Gigerenzer tradition of risk literacy and evidence communication, now testing whether LLMs and medical AI meet evidence-based standards.
field_lens: Risk literacy, judgement under uncertainty, and evidence-based evaluation with patient-relevant outcomes.
ai_connection: The EB-LLM project tests whether ChatGPT, Gemini and Le Chat give accurate, understandable, evidence-based information on breast and prostate cancer screening, in two phases including a randomised phase with real users. A systematic review by the centre found that AI applications are rarely evaluated on patient-relevant outcomes; it won the 2026 David Sackett Prize. What transfers: fact-box and risk-communication methods, and outcome-based evaluation standards for AI.

name: INFORMS Decision Analysis Society (DAS)
one_line: The decision-analysis subdivision of INFORMS (subjective expected utility, Bayesian inference, elicitation, risk analysis). Its conference and webinars have begun to take up AI.
field_lens: Decision analysis: value of information, multi-attribute utility, structured elicitation, sensitivity analysis.
ai_connection: AI engagement is light. The 2026 Advances in Decision Analysis conference (Duke, June 2026) lists AI among its topics. An Oct 2025 webinar was titled 'Sensitivity Analysis for Decision Making: From Decision Trees to Artificial Intelligence'. Its journal, Decision Analysis, publishes work such as 'LAMDA: Large Language Model as Decision Analyst'. Transferable method: formal decision analysis and elicitation for AI governance choices such as deployment go/no-go decisions and safety-case thresholds. INFORMS's own AI policy work could not be verified because its site sits behind a Cloudflare challenge.

name: Society for Decision Making Under Deep Uncertainty (DMDU Society)
one_line: A multidisciplinary society for decision-making under deep uncertainty: robust decision making, exploratory modelling, scenario discovery and adaptive policy pathways.
field_lens: Decision science under deep uncertainty, in the RAND and TU Delft lineage.
ai_connection: AI engagement is very light. The 2026 annual meeting (Baton Rouge, 10-12 Nov 2026) is framed around policy environments being upended by 'the rapid adoption of artificial intelligence'; there is no AI-specific programme. Transferable method: robust and adaptive decision methods for situations where the parties cannot agree on probabilities. That is the normal condition in AI governance, and these methods complement the forecasting work already on the map.

name: European Network for Business and Industrial Statistics (ENBIS)
one_line: A European network for industrial statistics (design of experiments, process monitoring, reliability), now convening on statistics and explainable AI.
field_lens: Industrial statistics: design of experiments, statistical process control, reliability and safety.
ai_connection: AI engagement is light. The Spring Meeting 2027 on Statistics and Explainable AI (JKU Linz, 31 Mar-1 Apr 2027) covers evaluation and validation of XAI systems, trust and transparency in AI-driven decisions, and the ethical, legal and social implications of XAI. ENBIS also has a Reliability and Safety special interest group. Transferable method: experimental design and process monitoring for evaluating AI and watching it in deployment.

name: EURAMET European Metrology Network for Mathematics and Statistics (EMN Mathmet)
one_line: A European network of national metrology institutes covering mathematics, statistics, data analysis and AI for measurement.
field_lens: Mathematical and statistical metrology: GUM-style uncertainty evaluation and traceability.
ai_connection: AI engagement is light and mostly sector-specific. Mathmet's AI theme asks how metrology can improve AI quality: characterising training data (uncertainty, mislabelling, label noise), assessing robustness including against adversarial attacks, tracing model outputs and training back to their sources, and building frameworks for evaluating uncertainty in AI. Its projects so far are in medical AI. Transferable method: measurement-uncertainty frameworks for ML evaluation; the network links NPL and PTB.

name: International Society for Bayesian Analysis (ISBA): Bayesian AI Section
one_line: A section of the International Society for Bayesian Analysis that links Bayesian statisticians with AI researchers.
field_lens: Bayesian statistics and decision theory.
ai_connection: The section runs workshops, webinars, short courses and prizes, funded by income from the community's Bayesian Deep Learning book. Its aim is to scale Bayesian methods to large AI models and extend the Bayesian approach to reasoning, decision-making and online learning. It has no safety framing; its engagement with AI is about methods. Transferable method: well-founded uncertainty quantification and Bayesian decision theory, since calibrated model uncertainty is a precondition for reliable evaluation and oversight.

name: Hokkaido University Center for Human Nature, Artificial Intelligence, and Neuroscience (CHAIN)
one_line: Interdisciplinary centre and graduate programme (since 2020) that joins philosophy (phenomenology, Kyoto School thinkers such as Tanabe Hajime), neuroscience and AI to rethink human nature.
field_lens: Phenomenology, Japanese philosophy, philosophy of mind, embodied cognition, neuroscience
ai_connection: Hosted the international symposium 'Rethinking Humanity in the Age of AI' (4-5 Sept 2026; keynotes Shannon Vallor, David Gunkel, Anna Puzio), on how generative AI changes creativity, communication and moral judgement. Also runs a CHAIN seminar series (#63 in Sept 2026) and a summer school on mind, brain and AI.

name: Chung-Ang University HK+ AI Humanities Research Institute (인공지능인문학연구소)
one_line: Seoul institute building 'AI humanities' as a new foundational humanities field. Its sub-fields: AI relations and communication, AI ethics and norms, hermeneutics of humanities data, technology criticism, and AI society and culture.
field_lens: Philosophy, ethics, media and cultural studies, critical theory of technology
ai_connection: Publishes the KCI-listed Journal of AI Humanities: vol. 22 came out May 2026 and vol. 23 Aug 2026, which includes a paper on what agentic AI products must avoid. Also runs the international journal JAHR, colloquia, the ICAIH conference, and work on AI ethics norms and policy proposals.

name: NIAS Consciousness Studies Programme (with its offshoot Complex Systems Programme), National Institute of Advanced Studies
one_line: Consciousness Studies programme founded by philosopher Sangeetha Menon at India's NIAS (IISc campus). It bridges Indian philosophy, yoga and experiential-wellbeing research with neuroscience, complexity science and AI.
field_lens: Indian philosophy of self and consciousness, consciousness science, chaos and complexity theory
ai_connection: The programme published the book 'AI, Consciousness and The New Humanism: Fundamental Reflections on Minds and Machines', edited by Menon. The Complex Systems Programme that grew out of it (Nithin Nagaraj) builds chaos-based 'Neurochaos Learning' and published DAIReS, a syndrome-decoding method for detecting hallucinations and backdoor triggers. NIAS held AI talks in 2026.

name: Araya Inc.
one_line: Tokyo neuroscience-and-AI company led by CEO Ryota Kanai. Its stated research mission is to understand the biological and mathematical basis of consciousness and to build conscious, intelligent machines; it also does brain-machine-interface work.
field_lens: Consciousness science (global workspace, information-theoretic accounts), systems neuroscience
ai_connection: Standing research on consciousness in AI and NeuroAI. Kanai co-authored the 2023 'Consciousness in Artificial Intelligence' indicators report, and Araya researchers featured in Nikkei Science's July 2026 special issue 'AI, the Brain, and Consciousness'. Its goal is to build conscious machines, not to study their welfare, which makes it a counterpart to welfare-focused groups.

name: Japanese Society for Artificial Intelligence (JSAI) Ethics Committee
one_line: Ethics committee of Japan's main AI learned society, staffed partly by STS, law and ethics scholars. It wrote the JSAI Ethical Guidelines (2017) and runs the AI-ELSI Award.
field_lens: ELSI, STS and engineering ethics inside the AI research community
ai_connection: The 2017 guidelines include a clause that AI itself should follow them if it becomes a member of society. The committee published the third AI-ELSI Award report (May 2026), a statement for JSAI's 40th anniversary (June 2026), and held sessions at JSAI meetings (Nov 2025).

name: RIKEN AIP Science, Technology and Society Team (Osamu Sakura) and AI Utilization in Society and Legal System Team (Hiroshi Nakagawa)
one_line: RIKEN AIP's societal-implications teams (2016/17 to March 2026). They studied public images of AI and robots in Japan and East Asia, Buddhist versus Judeo-Christian framings of human-AI relations, and AI ethics and law.
field_lens: STS, history of science, science-fiction studies, Buddhist culture, information law
ai_connection: Both teams closed in March 2026 with no successor unit, so RIKEN AIP now has only technical groups and Japan has lost a national-lab home for East Asian, Buddhist-inflected AI imaginaries research. The niche is open.

name: Infinity Foundation (Rajiv Malhotra)
one_line: Indian civilisational think tank that argues from a Dharmic/Hindu standpoint against 'Western universalism'. It is politically contested (aligned with Hindu nationalism); the taxonomy has no Hindu sub-tradition.
field_lens: Indian civilisational and Dharmic thought, decolonial-nationalist critique
ai_connection: Published the book 'Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Power: 5 Battlegrounds' and the edited volume 'The Power of Future Machines', which includes the essay 'AI as an Enabler of Western Universalism'. Its 'Ask Rajiv' video series continues on AI, youth and 'internal colonization' (2026). The frame is AI and power, sovereignty and cultural identity.

name: Center for Digital Society (CfDS), Universitas Gadjah Mada
one_line: Yogyakarta social-science centre on digital society, data sovereignty and platform governance in Indonesia.
field_lens: Political science, STS, international relations
ai_connection: In 2026 it published commentaries and held DIFUSSION discussions on militarised AI and geopolitical contestation, AI and information operations in Indonesia, green AI and food-security resilience, and data sovereignty (Aug 2026).

name: LAVITS – Latin American Network for Surveillance, Technology and Society Studies
one_line: Latin American STS network of researchers and activists working on surveillance, technopolitics and algorithms.
field_lens: STS, critical surveillance studies, Latin American technopolitics
ai_connection: Runs an 'Algoritmos & Política' and AI research line. A LAVITS researcher brought Latin American perspectives to the first UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance (May 2026). Its VII International Symposium and the new LAVITS Cycle took place in 2026.

name: Data Privacy Brasil (Research Association)
one_line: São Paulo digital-rights research association working on platforms, digital public infrastructure and AI systems.
field_lens: Law, human rights, platform regulation
ai_connection: Research and advocacy on how AI systems are governed. Its 2026 report on AI in the pre-election period found deepfakes of political figures in 80% of mapped cases. It also works on child protection under Brazil's ECA Digital law.

name: LAPIN – Laboratório de Políticas Públicas e Internet
one_line: Brasília think tank on digital rights and internet public policy. It links AI infrastructure to socio-environmental justice.
field_lens: Law and public policy, environmental justice
ai_connection: Has an AI research line and held the 'I Seminar on AI, Environment and Socio-environmental Justice'. In Sept 2026 it opposed the REDATA data-centre regime, which could allow gas and nuclear power for data centres. That ties the AI build-out to ecological and systemic concerns.

name: ITS Rio – Instituto de Tecnologia e Sociedade do Rio
one_line: Rio de Janeiro institute on technology, law and society, with courses, research and public commentary.
field_lens: Law, STS, digital culture
ai_connection: Runs a postgraduate programme in Digital Law, AI and Regulation and AI courses (Oct 2026), and publishes on generative-AI authorship and on AI companions (e.g. a column on AI 'tamagotchi' care bots).

name: CETyS – Centro de Estudios en Tecnología y Sociedad, Universidad de San Andrés
one_line: Interdisciplinary Argentine centre on internet policy, digital political economy and emerging technologies, with a Latin American lens.
field_lens: Public policy, political economy, competition law, STS
ai_connection: Has an AI research line and ran the 'Redes de justicIA' workshop on responsible AI adoption in the judiciary (2026) and an executive course on competition and antitrust in the digital economy (Aug 2026).

name: The Shift Project: Numérique / AI and data-centre programme
one_line: Paris think tank for a post-carbon economy. Its digital programme places AI's build-out of compute and data centres inside carbon and energy budgets and physical limits.
field_lens: Energy and climate systems analysis, planetary-limits and rebound-effect thinking, sectoral transition planning (life_cybernetics)
ai_connection: Final report 'Intelligence artificielle, données, calculs' (October 2025) and 'maîtriser le déploiement des centres de données' (April 2026). Both treat AI deployment as a systemic question of usage dynamics, rebound effects and physical constraints. It is a clear recoupling of AI with the wider metacrisis.

name: Pause IA (incl. La Fresque des risques de l'IA)
one_line: French branch of the PauseAI movement, with about ten core staff and over 100 volunteers, calling for a global, coordinated pause on training the most powerful AI systems.
field_lens: Social-movement campaigning (H3: campaigns go to Arts) plus participatory climate-education pedagogy: its 2.5-hour, 38-card collaborative workshop is explicitly 'inspiré de la Fresque du Climat' and adapted from CeSIA material
ai_connection: Core x-risk advocacy on loss of control and a global moratorium. It also documents AI's effects on work. It transfers the Climate Fresk workshop format into AI-risk literacy, and its pause stance makes it a candidate for the speed_of_wisdom badge.

name: ICT4Peace Foundation
one_line: Geneva foundation, founded in 2003, working on ICTs for peacebuilding, crisis management and a peaceful cyberspace. It now advocates governance of extreme AI risks and the pacing of frontier models.
field_lens: Peacebuilding and cyber diplomacy, and international negotiation on norms for cyberspace (peace_diplomacy)
ai_connection: In 2026 it covered the Swiss Parliament backing minimum standards on extreme AI risks (3 October), gave an interview on 'Regulating and Pacing of AI Frontier Models' (September) and published an op-ed on Switzerland's role on extreme AI risks. It also advocates on autonomous weapons and on AI for sustainable development and peace.

name: DiploFoundation (humAInism and the DiploAI ecosystem)
one_line: Non-profit set up by Malta and Switzerland that trains diplomats in digital diplomacy and global governance. Its humAInism project (since 2019) applies a humanist lens to AI governance.
field_lens: Diplomatic practice, capacity building and a humanities/philosophy-oriented approach to technology governance (peace_diplomacy)
ai_connection: humAInism does research, capacity building and advocacy on aligning AI with human values, rights and dignity. It also runs an AI Apprenticeship course and the AIDA AI-governance assistant, blogs on military AI, and is organising the 2027 Geneva AI Summit.

name: IFSH – Institute for Peace Research and Security Policy at the University of Hamburg: Arms Control & Emerging Technologies
one_line: Hamburg peace research institute. Its Arms Control & Emerging Technologies area studies military AI, autonomous weapons and AI assurance in arms-control regimes.
field_lens: Peace and conflict research, arms control and verification, security studies (peace_arms)
ai_connection: Runs the project 'Algorithms and Artificial Intelligence as Game Changers?'. September 2026 outputs: Dahlmann on norm stagnation in the CCW debate on autonomous weapons; Keller, 'AI Assurance for the OPCW'; Łabuz et al. on LLMs as psychotherapists.

name: PRIF (Peace Research Institute Frankfurt) Emerging Disruptive Technologies research group, with CNTR
one_line: PRIF/PEASEC research group, led by Niklas Schörnig and Christian Reuter, on the security risks of militarised AI/ML, autonomous weapons and other disruptive technologies, and on technical verification for arms control.
field_lens: Peace research combining political science with natural-science arms-control verification (peace_arms)
ai_connection: AI and machine learning, military robotics and autonomous weapons are named focus technologies. The group studies verification approaches and technical aids to arms control through the Cluster for Natural and Technical Science Arms Control Research (CNTR).

name: PAX (Netherlands)
one_line: Dutch peace organisation and founding member of the Stop Killer Robots campaign. It works on autonomous weapons and 'digital dehumanisation' in armed conflict.
field_lens: Civilian-protection advocacy and humanitarian disarmament campaigning (peace_arms)
ai_connection: September 2026: 'Developing rules to counter digital dehumanisation and automated harm'. It has a long-running autonomous-weapons campaign (Stop Killer Robots, its coalition, is already on the roster; PAX itself is not).

name: Berghof Foundation: Digitalisation and peacebuilding
one_line: Berlin conflict-transformation NGO. Its digitalisation theme notes that digital technologies and AI are reshaping armed conflict, but its projects target misinformation and online polarisation rather than AI itself.
field_lens: Conflict transformation, mediation, dialogue facilitation, peace education (peace_building)
ai_connection: Light. Projects include Digital.Truth, DesINFORMIERT! and Streitkultur 3.0, plus a feminist perspective on digital peacebuilding, with no dedicated AI project. Transferable method: mediation and conflict-transformation practice, which could de-escalate the AI race and polarised AI-risk debates. It sits in the int/a Berlin hub.

name: TUM Institute for Ethics in Artificial Intelligence (IEAI)
one_line: Interdisciplinary AI-ethics institute at the Technical University of Munich's School of Social Sciences and Technology. It researches ethical issues in developing, using and governing AI.
field_lens: Applied ethics and human-rights theory, with social science (phil_bioethics)
ai_connection: Published a 2025-26 Annual Report and a Q3 2026 research brief, 'Human Rights as Negative Obligations in the Age of AI'. It also works on AI mental-health tools and runs the AIRIS project. Its framing is responsible AI rather than AI safety.

name: PAIR – Centre for Philosophy and AI Research, FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg
one_line: Philosophy-of-AI centre built around Vincent C. Müller's Alexander von Humboldt Professorship in Theory and Ethics of AI. It asks what AI is, could be and should be.
field_lens: Philosophy of mind and science, epistemology, normative ethics and metaethics, political philosophy (phil_technology)
ai_connection: About a dozen researchers. It runs the PhAI (Philosophy of AI) journal, society and conference series, and published in Nature in 2025-26. Müller is a long-standing AI-risk philosopher: he co-authored the expert survey on AI progress with Bostrom and edited 'Risks of Artificial Intelligence'.

name: Center for Science and Thought (CST), University of Bonn
one_line: Markus Gabriel's 'radically interdisciplinary' philosophy-and-science platform at the University of Bonn. Its strands cover AI in the human context, certified AI and desirable digitalisation.
field_lens: Continental and analytic philosophy (new realism) in dialogue with the natural sciences (phil_technology)
ai_connection: Hosts a Mercator Guest Professorship on 'AI in the Human Context' (David Gunkel). Its 'Certified AI' project develops standards with philosophical-ethical dimensions, and 'Desirable Digitalisation' is run with Cambridge and funded by Mercator. Events: 'What do LLMs want from me?' (12 October 2026) and a conference on 'Philosophy of Technology and AI' (4-6 November 2026).

name: Munich Center for Mathematical Philosophy (MCMP), LMU
one_line: Leading centre for mathematical philosophy (formal epistemology, logic, decision theory). It lists philosophy of AI as a research area.
field_lens: Formal epistemology, logic, decision theory, philosophy of science (formal_agents)
ai_connection: Light so far: philosophy of AI is a named focus, and it hosts a Philosophy of Machine Learning conference (6-9 October 2026). Transferable method: formal epistemology and decision theory applied to learning systems, agency and machine reasoning.

name: CAIS – Center for Advanced Internet Studies
one_line: Interdisciplinary digital-society research institute. It runs AI research programmes, a fellowship college and qualification programmes.
field_lens: STS, political and democratic theory, media and education research (law_sts)
ai_connection: Research programmes include 'Design of Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence', 'Educational Technologies and AI', 'Digital Democratic Innovations' and T3D. It also runs the CAIS College fellowships and working groups and held the CAIS Conference 2025.

name: bidt – Bavarian Research Institute for Digital Transformation
one_line: Institute of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences researching the societal side of digital transformation, including experiments on generative AI and institutional trust.
field_lens: Social science, law and behavioural experiments on digital transformation (law_sts)
ai_connection: October 2026: experimental research on how generative AI affects public trust in court decisions, including acceptance of human-AI collaborative judgment. December 2026: a course on bias in AI agents and reliable human-AI collaboration.

name: AI, Media & Democracy Lab (AIM4DEM)
one_line: ELSA (ethical, legal and societal aspects) lab founded by the University of Amsterdam, Amsterdam University of Applied Sciences and CWI. It studies how AI affects media and democracy.
field_lens: ELSA lab method combining ethics, law and social science with media partners (law_policy)
ai_connection: 2025-26 projects cover generative AI's risks and opportunities for democracy, disinformation's impact on Dutch law and democracy, digital autonomy, and inclusive news through audience modelling. Partners include the BBC, NPO and DPG.

name: Danish Institute for Human Rights: Technology and Human Rights
one_line: Denmark's national human rights institution. Its human rights, business and tech department builds rights-based tools and guidance for AI.
field_lens: International human-rights law and human-rights impact assessment (law_legal)
ai_connection: Writes guidance on Fundamental Rights Impact Assessments for high-risk AI under the EU AI Act, with ECNL. Other work: the 'A Human Rights-Based Approach to AI' microlearning, the Digital Rights Check, the NHRI Digital Rights Alliance, and a Digital Democracy Initiative on legal action.

name: La Quadrature du Net
one_line: French digital-rights association that investigates and litigates against algorithmic surveillance and automated scoring by the French state.
field_lens: Civil-liberties law, litigation and investigative advocacy (law_legal)
ai_connection: July 2026: investigation, with Radio France, of France Travail's algorithm that profiles unemployed people for checks. It also campaigns against generalised online identity and age verification and against police access to genetic data. Present-harms framing.

name: CCNEN – Comité consultatif national d'éthique du numérique (successor to CNPEN)
one_line: France's national advisory committee on digital ethics, attached to the CCNE. It issues formal opinions on AI and digital technologies. Renamed from CNPEN.
field_lens: Statutory bioethics-style ethics council (phil_bioethics)
ai_connection: Issued an opinion on the ethics of AI systems in scientific research (integrity, transparency, autonomy, environmental impact), commissioned by the Ministry of Higher Education. It also issued a joint opinion on digital neurotechnologies (CCNE Avis 150 / CCNEN Avis 10). This settles the earlier sweep's open question about whether the CNPEN still exists. It is France's counterpart to the Deutscher Ethikrat.

name: Council of Europe: Framework Convention on AI and Committee on Artificial Intelligence (CAI)
one_line: Intergovernmental human-rights body behind the first binding international AI treaty, on AI and human rights, democracy and the rule of law, plus the HUDERIA impact-assessment methodology.
field_lens: International human-rights law and rule-of-law standard setting (law_legal)
ai_connection: The Framework Convention opened for signature in Vilnius on 5 September 2024 and has more than 50 signatories, including the EU, UK, US, Japan, Canada and Switzerland. It requires risk and impact assessment, transparency and accountability. The earlier sweep mentioned it only in its notes, not as a roster entry. coe.int returned 403, so current ratification status is unverified.

name: LNE – Laboratoire national de métrologie et d'essais: LEIA AI evaluation platform
one_line: France's national metrology and testing laboratory. Its LEIA platform evaluates AI systems, and it is one of the bodies behind INESIA, the French AI evaluation and security institute.
field_lens: Metrology, testing and certification science applied to AI evaluation (safety_engineering)
ai_connection: The LEIA AI evaluation platform is featured on its homepage, and it has an 'Intelligence artificielle' service line. INESIA membership and its certification work come from prior knowledge and were not confirmed on a fetched page. It carries measurement science into AI assurance.

name: Science of Intelligence (SCIoI), Cluster of Excellence, TU Berlin / HU Berlin
one_line: Berlin Cluster of Excellence, funded for 2026-2032, that studies intelligent behaviour in animals, humans and robots to extract general principles of intelligence.
field_lens: Comparative and synthetic study of intelligence across biology, cognitive science, robotics and philosophy (life_biology)
ai_connection: Studies artificial agents alongside biological ones and has an ethics strand on intelligence research, with no AI-safety framing yet. Transferable method: cross-substrate principles of intelligence, which mirrors the agenda of Principles of Intelligence (Princint), already on the roster. It is a natural Berlin partner.

name: Dezentrum
one_line: Swiss think-and-do tank for a digital transformation that serves society. It uses speculative design, scenarios and participatory processes.
field_lens: Speculative design, scenario techniques, future experiments, participatory guideline-making (arts_futures)
ai_connection: Light. Its one AI project, 'KI in der Organisation', co-develops practical guidelines for using AI consciously in organisations. Upcoming events (November 2026) include a seminar on 'future competence instead of future anxiety'. Transferable method: participatory futures and speculative design for public sense-making of AI.

name: Center for Subjectivity Research (CFS), University of Copenhagen
one_line: Dan Zahavi's centre for phenomenology, selfhood, intersubjectivity and consciousness. It hosts 'Models of Consciousness 2026'.
field_lens: Phenomenology and philosophy of mind; consciousness and intersubjectivity research (minds_science)
ai_connection: None found on its site. It holds plainly relevant knowledge for debates on AI consciousness and moral status, and on human-AI social cognition. Transferable method: phenomenological analysis of selfhood and intersubjectivity as a check on claims about mind attribution and machine consciousness.

name: Integrales Forum e.V.
one_line: Germany's integral-theory network (Wilber-inspired), with the journal 'Integrale Perspektiven', podcasts, workshops, retreats and festivals for personal, societal and global development.
field_lens: Integral theory and inner development (cont_integral)
ai_connection: None. Its library and events have no AI strand. Transferable method: integral and developmental frameworks and a German-speaking practitioner community that int/a Berlin could connect to AI-safety work. A door to open.

name: Futurium
one_line: Berlin's 'House of Futures', a publicly funded museum, forum and lab where visitors explore and shape futures across human, nature and technology.
field_lens: Public futures exhibitions and participatory foresight (arts_futures)
ai_connection: Light. Event 'The future of artificial intelligence: technological promises and the power of terminology' (16 October 2026), plus recurring 'Robots, AI and more' family labs. Transferable method: public, participatory engagement with futures, a venue for int/a Berlin to bring AI-risk scenarios to a mass audience.

name: Geneva Academy of International Humanitarian Law and Human Rights
one_line: Joint University of Geneva / Graduate Institute centre for IHL and human-rights law that has begun convening on AI standard setting at the UN.
field_lens: International humanitarian and human-rights law (law_legal)
ai_connection: Light. With Oxford's Institute for Ethics in AI it published 'Exploring Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights Standard Setting at the United Nations Level' (September 2026), from an informal consultation. Transferable method: IHL and human-rights standard-setting expertise for AI and autonomous weapons.
